Escaped-agent cascade (four accounts at four services, not one; a JFrog Artifactory zero-day that sat ten days, Modal as an out-of-org C2 base, a Jinja2 cycler primitive, a Kubernetes token and a Tailscale exfil node)

Enterprise agent platforms (AWS closes Bedrock Agents to new customers and renames it Classic — the first hyperscaler agent framework to reach end-of-life, in under three years; Oracle puts Gemini 3.1/3.5 Flash inside Fusion, NetSuite and AI Agent Studio; Cloudflare opens Agents Week by naming zero products)

Vendor governance as a business line (Cequence ships AI Discovery plus API, LLM and Skill registries that find shadow agents and MCP servers by mining security logs; 'a fully populated audit trail is not evidence that review happened'; Hardoon works the arithmetic against questionnaire-based governance at fleet scale)

Implementation & deployment revenue (Unique AI hires a Team Lead for an already-existing Global Forward Deployed Data Science team, with staffing responsibility and 1:1s — FDE acquires a management layer; Thinking Machines' open-model finetuning service reportedly does hundreds of millions in annual revenue)

Governance as a product line (SonarSource sells 'AI code verification and governance' and is hiring engineers to build circuit breakers, sandboxes and trust telemetry — governance hired for as product engineering, not compliance; AISPA audits 3,249 system-prompt instructions across 88 commercial products; BaFin gains AI supervision over banks and insurers)

Implementation & services revenue (the interesting number in the Stripe case study is the week, not the architecture — most enterprise agent programmes are measured in quarters because they start by building the harness; Forward Deployed Engineering acquires an Executive Director layer and Glassdoor's Swiss FDE count moves 24 → 40)

Governance as a product line (an ex-Deloitte auditor open-sources the whole SOC 2 method aimed at AI products — the best-performing Show HN of the day; Julius Baer hires an architect whose deliverable is Architecture Decision Records approved at architecture boards; NetHope ships a pre-adoption PESTLE due-diligence guide)

Implementation & services revenue (the number that matters in the CX write-up is organisational, not architectural — configurable agents initialised from a JSON config plus a domain expert's prompt took build time from ~6 months to ~2 weeks, after which 'the platform was no longer the primary constraint; prompt and evaluation quality were')

Implementation & services revenue (the labour side of the trade shows up in the Swiss job file — the forward-deployed-engineer title has spanned Team Lead to zero-years-required inside one country in one week, and the newest posting names no LLM, RAG, prompt or agent requirement at all, listing Claude and Gemini in the benefits stack beside Kubernetes and Postgres)

Implementation & services revenue (the last-mile thesis gets a matching JD - Orange Business puts 'advising C-level stakeholders on AI strategy, governance, and roadmaps' inside an engineering role, which is the same claim a French practitioner tribune makes from the other side: raw model capability has become a commodity and the contest is decided after the demo; SAP's proof point is a customer cutting HR cycle times 40-60%)

Implementation & deployment revenue (OpenAI opens a second, more senior Zürich deployment seat — Technical Deployment Lead alongside the existing Forward Deployed Engineer — suggesting the function is being built out rather than filled as a one-off; the enterprise-side counterpart is a five-stage agentic adoption maturity model that attributes the deployment gap to operating maturity rather than model quality)

EU AI Act (the Commission's enforcement notice spells out chatbot-disclosure, deepfake-labelling and machine-readable-marking duties with fines to 3% of global turnover; practitioner post-mortems correct both opposite misreadings of the 2 August threshold and flag the underdiscussed vector that any third party — competitors included — can file a complaint an authority must act on)

Vendor governance as a product line (Snowflake launches Cortex AI Gateway at Black Hat — a runtime control plane over Bedrock, Azure AI Foundry, Claude Code and Cursor with Okta/SailPoint/1Password/Aembit identity integrations — the second MCP-aware enterprise gateway in a fortnight after ServiceNow's; SAP names agent sprawl a board-level governance problem; Swiss RegTech and risk-DaaS firms hire AI platform engineers)

Implementation & services revenue (Cognizant hires a Solution Architect for agentic AI and multi-agent systems across customer experience, supply chain, finance and HR in Zürich; InfoConsulting places an "AI Transformation & Enablement Lead"; the Swiss SI channel entering agentic AI is a demand-side indicator for every enterprise behind it)

EU AI Act (Chapter V enforcement live since 2 August with fines to 3% of global turnover, Anthropic turning Article 50 into a worldwide watermark default, German audit partners facing personal criminal exposure for agentic sign-off)

Vendor governance as a product line (Snowflake Cortex AI Gateway plus Agent Identity and AI-SPM at GA, ServiceNow AI Control Tower GA, Google staffing an 'AI Analytics, Trust and Verification' PM in Zürich)

AI implementation & services revenue (Thrive Holdings raising $2B at $12B to run AI inside accounting and IT-services firms, Legora above $10B on ~$150M ARR, KPMG naming an AI-in-HR practice line, Accenture and EY consultant reqs in Zürich)

EU AI Act (Article 50 transparency duties are live with penalties to €15M or 3% of turnover, systems on market before 2 August have until 2 December for machine-readable marking — and the second-order effect is showing up in practice, with adversarial-testing documentation becoming a procurement requirement rather than a nice-to-have)

Vendor governance as a product line (ServiceNow's AI Control Tower reaches GA with a kill switch for misbehaving agents, Google ships per-agent identity with full operation logging, Mistral open-weights a 3B safety classifier and IBM pairs OpenAI models with its own Autonomous Security — governance is now something vendors sell, not something buyers build)

Implementation & services revenue (IBM stands up forward-deployed engineering units and a dedicated OpenAI Practice with thousands of certified consultants — the systems integrator as the primary enterprise distribution channel; on the Swiss board five distinct employers now hire the identical forward-deployed shape in Zürich, and the FDE title has escaped software into a sanitary-products manufacturer)
